name: GitHub Actions
description: Protects against destructive GitHub Actions operations like deleting secrets/variables \ or using gh api DELETE against /actions endpoints.

destructive_patterns.name: gh-actions-secret-remove
destructive_patterns.description: gh secret delete/remove deletes GitHub Actions secrets. This can break CI and may be hard to recover.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a GitHub Actions secret removes it from the repository, organization, \ or environment. Workflows using this secret will fail with authentication or \ configuration errors. Secret values are not recoverable after deletion.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - gh secret list: Review existing secrets first \ - Update the secret value instead of deleting \ - Check workflow files for secret usage before removing

destructive_patterns.name: gh-actions-variable-remove
destructive_patterns.description: gh variable delete/remove deletes GitHub Actions variables. This can break workflows.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Removing a GitHub Actions variable makes it unavailable to all workflows that \ reference it. Unlike secrets, variable values are visible, but workflows may \ fail with undefined variable errors after deletion.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - gh variable list: Review existing variables first \ - gh variable set: Update value instead of removing \ - Search workflows for variable usage before removing

destructive_patterns.name: gh-actions-workflow-disable
destructive_patterns.description: gh workflow disable disables workflows. This is reversible, but can disrupt CI.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Disabling a workflow prevents it from running on any triggers. This is reversible \ with 'gh workflow enable', but can disrupt CI/CD pipelines, scheduled jobs, and \ automated deployments while disabled.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - gh workflow list: Review workflow status first \ - gh workflow view: Check workflow details \ - Use workflow_dispatch for manual control instead

destructive_patterns.name: gh-actions-run-cancel
destructive_patterns.description: gh run cancel cancels a running workflow. This is reversible, but may disrupt deployments.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Canceling a workflow run stops it mid-execution. Any in-progress deployments, \ tests, or builds will be interrupted. The run can be re-triggered, but partial \ work may leave systems in an inconsistent state.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - gh run view: Check run status and progress first \ - gh run list: Review running workflows \ - Wait for natural completion if possible

destructive_patterns.name: gh-actions-api-delete-secrets
destructive_patterns.description: gh api DELETE against /actions/secrets deletes GitHub Actions secrets.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Making DELETE requests to the GitHub Actions secrets API removes secrets from \ the repository. This bypasses CLI confirmations and directly modifies repository \ settings. Workflows will fail when referencing deleted secrets.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Use gh secret delete for safer deletion with prompts \ - gh api GET first: Verify secret exists \ - Prefer CLI commands over direct API calls

destructive_patterns.name: gh-actions-api-delete-variables
destructive_patterns.description: gh api DELETE against /actions/variables deletes GitHub Actions variables.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Making DELETE requests to the GitHub Actions variables API removes variables \ from the repository. This bypasses CLI confirmations and directly modifies \ repository settings. Workflows referencing these variables will fail.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Use gh variable delete for safer deletion with prompts \ - gh api GET first: Verify variable exists \ - Prefer CLI commands over direct API calls
